high.title: Indonesia Receives US$17 Billion Commitment from AIIB, Finance Minister Says It's Not Debt
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has secured a US$17 billion (approximately Rp303 trillion) financing commitment from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a China-backed multilateral lender. The minister clarified that this is project financing rather than sovereign debt, intended for productive infrastructure projects with below-market interest rates, with funds accessible through 2029. This is a significant capital inflow development that could affect Indonesia's infrastructure pipeline and fiscal outlook.

high.title: Trump Furious, US Strikes Iran Again — Threat to Strait of Hormuz Oil Trade
high.summary: The United States has launched new military strikes against Iran, targeting missile storage facilities, drone sites, and coastal radar installations, after accusing Iran of violating a ceasefire agreement over the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil shipping route, and renewed conflict poses significant risks to global energy prices and supply chains. Indonesian investors should monitor potential impacts on global oil prices, domestic fuel costs, and related energy stocks.

high.title: Finance Minister Confirms Significant Budget Cuts to Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) Program
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that the government will implement significant budget efficiency cuts to the flagship Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program, stating he personally wished the budget could be reduced to zero but acknowledged the program's social value. The minister emphasized that implementation quality must improve and that the cuts will make Indonesia's overall budget position safer. This signals ongoing fiscal consolidation efforts that may affect government spending patterns and related food/nutrition sector suppliers.

high.title: US Military Strikes Iran After Singapore Ship Shot in Strait of Hormuz
high.summary: The US military launched strikes against Iran on Friday (June 26), targeting missile storage sites, drone facilities, and coastal radar positions, in retaliation for Iran's attack on a Singapore vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz. This escalation poses a significant threat to global oil supply chains, as the Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for energy shipments. Indonesian businesses and investors should monitor potential impacts on oil prices and regional shipping costs.

high.title: Trump Threatens 100% Tariffs on Countries That Tax US Digital Companies
high.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a 100% retaliatory tariff threat against any country imposing digital services taxes on US tech companies, stating the measure would replace existing trade agreements. This policy could significantly impact Indonesia, which has been developing its own digital tax framework, and may jeopardize ongoing trade negotiations with the US. Indonesian exporters and the tech sector face heightened uncertainty as this threat could disrupt bilateral trade relations.

high.title: Iran Issues Stern Warning to Ships Navigating Outside Official Strait of Hormuz Routes
high.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) warned all vessels to strictly follow Tehran-designated shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening action against ships using unauthorized lanes. This move signals Iran's intent to maintain control over one of the world's most critical oil transit corridors, even amid existing US-Iran peace agreements. For Indonesian shipping companies and energy importers, this creates heightened operational risk and uncertainty around freight costs and supply chain reliability.

high.title: Trump Furious: US Strikes Iran Again After Alleged Ceasefire Violation in Strait of Hormuz
high.summary: The US launched military strikes against Iranian missile storage sites, drone facilities, and coastal radar installations on June 25, citing Iran's alleged violation of the Strait of Hormuz ceasefire agreement. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical global oil trade route, and renewed conflict there poses significant risks to global oil supply and energy prices. Indonesian investors should monitor potential spikes in oil prices and their impact on Indonesia's energy sector and current account balance.

high.title: Indonesia Secures US$17 Billion in Funding from AIIB — Finance Minister Says It's Not Debt
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced a US$17 billion (approximately IDR 303 trillion) project financing commitment from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a China-backed multilateral lender headquartered in Beijing. The minister clarified the funds are structured as project financing rather than sovereign debt, targeting productive infrastructure projects with lower interest rates than commercial investors, with disbursements available through 2029. This is a significant capital inflow for Indonesian infrastructure development and could boost investment activity across multiple sectors.

medium.title: Coal Supply for State Utility PLN Revealed: 141 Million Metric Tons Secured Out of 154 Million Needed
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) disclosed that approximately 141 million metric tons of coal have been secured for state electricity company PLN out of a total annual requirement of 154 million metric tons. The ministry had temporarily halted some coal exports to prioritize domestic energy supply, but exports have since returned to normal. This update is relevant for investors in Indonesian coal and energy stocks, as domestic market obligation (DMO) enforcement and export restrictions can materially impact coal producer revenues.

medium.title: MRT Route from Lebak Bulus to Serpong Kept Secret to Prevent Land Speculation
medium.summary: Indonesia's Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi confirmed that the exact route of the planned MRT extension from Lebak Bulus to Serpong, South Tangerang, will not be disclosed publicly until closer to project execution, in order to prevent land brokers from inflating property prices along the corridor. The feasibility study for the project is targeted for completion by end of 2026. This is relevant for property and infrastructure investors monitoring development corridors in the Greater Jakarta area.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Rises Slightly, Buyback Price Jumps by IDR 38,000 per Gram
medium.summary: Antam's 24-karat gold price rose IDR 5,000 per gram to IDR 2,660,000 after two days of stagnation, while the buyback price saw a sharper jump of IDR 38,000 per gram. Over the past week, Antam gold has traded in the range of IDR 2,655,000–2,673,000 per gram, reflecting modest but positive momentum. This is relevant for retail investors holding gold as a safe-haven asset amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya on Free Nutritious Meal Program Budget Efficiency: 'I Wanted Zero, But That's Not Possible'
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed significant budget cuts to the government's Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program, stating the reduction is 'quite significant' and will help stabilize state finances. While acknowledging the program's social value, he urged the National Nutrition Agency (BGN) to improve implementation efficiency. This signals continued fiscal consolidation efforts by the government, which may reassure bond market participants but raises questions about the program's long-term funding sustainability.

medium.title: Coal Supply Situation for State Electricity Company PLN Revealed: 141 Million Metric Tons Secured Out of 154 Million Needed
medium.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) disclosed that 141 million metric tons of coal have been secured for PLN's annual requirement of 154 million metric tons, leaving a gap of approximately 13 million metric tons. The ministry had temporarily halted coal exports to prioritize domestic energy supply for PLN's power plants before resuming normal export activity. This development is relevant for investors in Indonesia's coal mining sector as it highlights ongoing domestic market obligations (DMO) enforcement and temporary export restrictions.

medium.title: MRT Lebak Bulus–Serpong Route Kept Secret to Prevent Land Speculation
medium.summary: Indonesia's Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi confirmed that the exact route for the planned MRT extension from Lebak Bulus to Serpong, South Tangerang, will remain confidential until project execution to prevent land price speculation and scalping. The feasibility study for the project is targeted for completion by end of 2026, with social media speculation already pointing to potential corridors through Pondok Aren or Pondok Cabe. Property investors and developers in the South Tangerang corridor should watch for official route announcements, which could significantly impact land values in the affected areas.
